name: Albania
summary: Albania has the fastest-growing electric-car fleet in the region: Eurostat counts 10,938 battery-electric passenger cars at the end of 2025, 91% more than a year earlier, most of them imported used cars. New electric vehicles are VAT-exempt and pay no annual vehicle tax. Public charging is young and fragmented: VEGA runs 20+ sites, PlugoAL five 280 kW sites, and the state supplier OSHEE plans a national network in 2026. No network publishes a per-kWh price on its website; OSHEE says drivers typically pay 40–60 lek per kWh. At home, a kilowatt-hour costs 10.2 lek with VAT.

stats.label: Registered road vehicles, 2025
stats.note: Passenger cars are 80.8% of all vehicles; 72.1% of passenger cars run on diesel.

public_count.note: No official register exists. OSHEE also says about 16,000 electric vehicles were registered at that time — a wider definition than Eurostat's battery-electric passenger cars. Open Charge Map lists 15 locations and OpenStreetMap about 75 objects.

networks.name: VEGA Charging
networks.size: 20+ sites, mostly at fuel stations (Gega Oil, Kastrati and others) on the Tirana–Durrës–Fier–Vlorë–Sarandë and Shkodër routes; GB/T and CCS2 connectors

networks.name: PlugoAL
networks.size: 5 sites with 280 kW chargers (Tirana, Durrës, Vlorë, Gjirokastër, Shkodër)

networks.name: OSHEE Charge (planned)
networks.size: 100–120 sites planned in the first phase, within 2026

networks.name: iCharge
networks.size: Platform used by several station owners; not a single operator

prices.price: shown in the app before charging

electricity.what: Households, up to 700 kWh a month
electricity.note: ERE table for 1 January–31 December 2026. One price per block, no day/night difference.

electricity.price: 9.5 lek/kWh without VAT (11.4 with VAT) for the whole month's consumption
electricity.note: An EV that pushes a household over 700 kWh makes the whole month dearer: for 200 kWh of charging this can work out at about 14.7 lek per EV kWh (our calculation).
OSHEE's estimate; operators buy electricity for chargers above 11 kW at 22 lek/kWh (25.3 at peak) under an ERE decision from 01.11.2025.

subsidies.programme: VAT exemption for new battery-electric vehicles
subsidies.amount: 20% VAT not charged at import or first sale
subsidies.who: Buyers of new, never-registered battery-electric vehicles (not used EVs or hybrids)
subsidies.note: Customs duty on cars consists only of VAT, so a new EV is imported tax-free.

subsidies.note: We could not confirm that the refund still applies in 2026.

buildings.text: We found no EV-specific rule for chargers in apartment buildings in Albania.

policy.text: The draft National Energy and Climate Plan aims for 10% of vehicles in circulation to be electric by 2030.
The Albanian Energy Efficiency Agency tendered the installation and operation of public chargers (83.3 million lek) in 2023.

gaps: No network publishes a per-kWh price on its website; prices are in the apps.
Site counts per network could not be verified in Open Charge Map (API blocked).
The GB/T connector share among imported Chinese EVs is not documented; VEGA's GB/T sockets suggest demand.
No fast charger on the A1 (Rruga e Kombit) itself was confirmed.
